newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end weak, U.S. holiday dampens trade.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end weak, U.S. holiday dampens trade.

text.p: 1617 MT - UK gilts end Monday's session in the red, easing back in trade muted by a holiday in the U.S.. Market awaits clutch of key data due later in the week. BoE auction details main market focus on Tuesday. * March gilt futures 4/32 lower at 113-08. * March short sterling unchanged at 93.70.
"The main question for the market at the moment is what the Bank will go for in its details tomorrow," said a gilts trader at a U.S. bank in London.
The Bank of England is due to announce details on Tuesday for February 25's long-dated gilt auction.
Dealers said the favoured view in the market was that the Bank would opt for a new tranche of the existing 8.0 percent gilts due 2021.
"We think the 8.0 percent due 2021 is the sensible choice and if they do go for that, it shouldn't hold any surpises for the market," said one.
He said domestic investors, "flushed with cash and looking for buying opportunities", would be keen to snap up the new tranche and flatten the yield curve.
Data coming up this week include January public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) figures on Tuesday, and January retail sales on Wednesday.

But analysts said that unless any particularly unwelcome surprises were hidden in the data, the gilt market would remain well supported and maintain the view that interest rates are on hold until the election.
